html:
The rapidly escalating tensions and military posturing in the Middle East largely shape the world order today, as Iran issues stern warnings against US attacks and outlines conditions for reopening the vital Strait of Hormuz amidst an ongoing war. The US, in turn, cautions against swift regional escalation, underscoring the precarious geopolitical climate.

US-Iran & Regional Instability: Iran has conveyed seven conditions to the US for potential negotiations and explicitly warned of "painful" and "unlimited" retaliation if US aggression resumes, simultaneously raising its military preparedness to the highest level across air, ground, and naval domains. Tehran claims the US and regional countries agreed in Europe to renew war against them, asserting that countries siding with the US would become targets. This comes as Saudi Arabia reports that Yemen's Houthi rebels tried to attack Riyadh with a ballistic missile, and Iranian Armed Forces spokesperson Abolfazl Shekarchi stated Iran still holds the initiative in the Strait of Hormuz, contradicting US claims. Separately, Iran executed a man accused of spying for Israel's Mossad. The US Mission to the UAE and the US Department of State have urged Americans to reconsider travel to the Middle East, citing the unpredictable situation and potential for escalation.

Russia-Ukraine & European Security: Ukraine launched its "largest ever" drone attack on Moscow, with hundreds of drones downed and three people reported dead, coinciding with the final day of Russia's parliamentary elections. Russia's ruling United Russia party is projected to win the wartime vote. Meanwhile, France, Poland, and other European nations express alarm over escalating Russian "hybrid" attacks, while Ukraine steps up measures to protect its railway infrastructure from increased Russian assaults.

Great Power Realignment & Technology: A crucial summit this week between Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping will focus on defining global leadership in artificial intelligence, with US and Chinese officials already discussing a mechanism for communicating over serious AI incidents. Domestically, Trump reportedly plans to form a health funding board that could veto "woke" initiatives and announced plans to create an 'AI Force' and appoint an AI czar. Elsewhere, French President Emmanuel Macron and Canadian leader Mark Carney have pledged closer ties, meeting in a French territory off Canada amid "Trump tensions" and Canada's ongoing trade war with the US, with Macron supporting Canada as an EU associate member. In Germany, Chancellor Merz called state election losses a "disaster" for his party, though he vows to stay on.

Economic Ripple Effects & Middle East Tensions: Global oil prices hit over a one-week low on hopes of a boost to diplomacy in the Iran war, though Reuters notes concerns over an earlier drone hit on a Saudi pipeline that will keep it out of service for weeks, further restricting oil flow. Fuel prices in Lebanon have also jumped significantly, with a kiloliter of mazout increasing by $127 in one week, attributed to the war in the Middle East. Meanwhile, violence continues in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, with an Israeli reportedly shot dead in the occupied West Bank, and the Gaza death toll rising to 73,910. Jordan and Qatar condemned the storming of Al-Aqsa Mosque by an Israeli minister and settlers.

Global Challenges & Domestic Issues: Australia's seventh intergenerational report projects a future of lower economic growth, with more Australians dying than being born in 40 years, while also highlighting the uncertain age of artificial intelligence. In Ethiopia, the country's main armed groups announced an alliance against the government. In other news, the sister of Pakistan's ex-PM Imran Khan, Aleema Khanum, was arrested on accusations of mobilizing supporters for protests.
